Makrele.et: From Middle High German makrēle, from Middle Low German makkerēle, from Middle Dutch makereel, from Old French maquerel. Further origin unknown. Compare modern Dutch makreel, modern French maquereau, English mackerel.

Makake.et: Borrowed from French macaque, from Portuguese macaco, of uncertain origin.

makaber.et: From French macabre, through Spanish macabro and possibly Arabic مَقَابِر (maqābir, “cemeteries”), plural of مَقْبَرَة (maqbara).

Makron.et: Borrowed from Ancient Greek μακρόν (makrón, “long”, neuter singular).

Makadam.et: Borrowed from English macadam, named after Scottish engineer John Loudon McAdam (1756–1836).

Maki.et: Borrowed from French maki, from Malagasy maky (“ring-tailed lemur”).
